title: An Engineering Neuro-Fuzzy Decision Support System for Optimizing an Industrial Sulfur Production Process Under Uncertainty
abstract: Sulfur recovery units (SRUs) at oil refineries are complex, multi-parameter systems whose Cold Bed Absorption (CBA) reactors operate under incomplete and uncertain process information, which limits conventional control. This study develops an engineering neuro-fuzzy decision support system (DSS) for optimizing sulfur production at the Atyrau oil refinery (Kazakhstan) under uncertainty. The system integrates a mathematical description of the process, whose dynamic part is stated as a general formulation, an expert-derived fuzzy rule base, a first-order Sugeno neuro-fuzzy estimator of sulfur yield and quality, and a multi-criteria fuzzy optimization block based on the Bellman–Zadeh approach, together with an explicit operator-facing decision algorithm and a software interface. The estimators were identified and validated on 200 operating log records of the unit. These records show that the effect of reactor temperature on the sulfur quality index reverses sign with reactor pressure—the correlation is −0.57 below 0.79 kgf/cm2 and +0.75 above it—so that a model additive in the two variables cannot represent the relationship: linear regression on temperature and pressure attains a cross-validated R2 of only 0.06 for the quality index, whereas the neuro-fuzzy estimator attains 0.83 (RMSE 0.72 points, MAPE 0.74%). A regression with an explicit interaction term on the same inputs attains 0.79; in a paired comparison the neuro-fuzzy estimator had the lower error in every repetition, but the difference is not statistically significant (p = 0.07), and the estimator is retained for its rule-level interpretability and its integration with the decision block. For sulfur yield, where the relationship is close to linear once pressure and throughput are accounted for, the corresponding figures are 0.71 and 0.85 (RMSE 0.33 t/day, MAPE 1.35%). The same ordering is reproduced on an independent hold-out test set, under nested and cluster-blocked cross-validation and after removal of the records lying at the unit’s capacity and regulatory bounds, and the expert rule base was revised into an asymmetric form accordingly. A worked application of the optimization block to three operating situations, with the production plan, quality and capacity constraints enforced, raised the model-predicted degree of joint satisfaction of the yield, quality and energy criteria from 0.08–0.25 to 0.49–0.57; in one of the three, the recommended action is to reduce process severity and lower a reheat duty surrogate by about a third rather than to increase output. The resulting DSS, at present a standalone advisory software prototype, supports the operator in analyzing the current process state, evaluating alternative operating modes and forming recommendations, while the final decision remains with the operator.

title: Designing Adaptive Affective Chatbots for Online Learning: Insights from an Iterative Design Study
abstract: Online students often face emotional challenges such as frustration, isolation, and fluctuating motivation, which can hinder sustained engagement in online learning. While much work on learning support chatbots has focused primarily on cognitive assistance, affective and motivational support remains underexplored in online learning contexts. We present an iterative user-centered design study investigating how adaptive affective chatbots can better support learners facing these challenges. A mixed-methods needfinding study with graduate CS students (survey n=38; interviews n=4) revealed substantial variation in learner preferences for affective support, which informed the development of three adaptive design alternatives: user-controlled, AI-driven, and hybrid co-controlled adaptation. Through formative evaluation (n=25), we identified key trade-offs between automation, transparency, and user control, informing the refinement of a hybrid design. A final evaluation (n=25) showed that 88.0% (22/25) of participants preferred the hybrid design, highlighting the value of balancing transparency, learner control, and interaction simplicity. Our findings provide design implications for adaptive affective chatbot systems that support emotionally challenging online learning contexts.

title: A Reproducible Data-Processing and Evaluation Framework for Federated Agricultural Knowledge Repositories
abstract: Agricultural bibliographic catalogs are difficult to benchmark for distributed learning because the records remain at the centers that produced them. We process 75,897 records from the International System for Agricultural Science and Technology (AGRIS), held by seven area-prefix clients, into a federated multi-view benchmark with four disjoint views (1096 features) and ten AGROVOC classes. Publication-level grouping precedes a client- and class-stratified 70/10/20 split; without it, 1132 duplicate-document groups would have crossed folds. In a blinded 400-record audit, the heuristic agreed with the consensus labels for 94.50% of the records (macro-F1 0.945; sampling-weighted accuracy 94.91%). On one shared schedule and a pre-specified budget of 40 rounds, federated averaging (FedAvg) reaches a macro-F1 of 0.2998±0.0151, below centralized training (0.4123±0.0066) and local-only training (0.4020±0.0175). Its validation curve has not converged by round 40, so the gap is a budget result, not a property of a fully trained model. FedProx and 8-bit quantization (0.3001±0.0147) stay within the seed-to-seed variation of FedAvg; quantization reduces uplink traffic 4-fold (total traffic 1.6-fold). The contribution is the benchmark and its evaluation protocol. Zenodo release v1.2 supports recomputation of the reported results and, when the AGRIS files match the stored checksums, reconstruction of the source text.

title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
abstract: GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. Reported systems differ in harness and test subset and often change several designs at once, so it is hard to tell which choices produce the gains. We take these designs apart and test them in one framework, along the harness around the model, the action interface, the reuse of experience and the scene geometry given to the model. A lean harness that keeps the full episode history and stops each motion early goes a long way. Reusing experience changes how the model acts but is not a free lunch, and scene geometry helps most, even when depth is predicted from RGB alone. JustRUA starts from the official L3 harness and keeps only what matters most. Even with no learned policy, self-improvement loop or task-specific tuning, this simple harness raises the score on the RoboDojo simulation benchmark substantially, from 29.7 to 50.3.

title: Content-Conditioned Invariant Feature-Statistic Augmentation: Unifying Robustness and Weight Averaging for Domain Generalization
abstract: Domain generalization aims to learn a reliable predictor on unseen target domains from source domains alone. Traditional empirical risk minimization (ERM), which relies on spurious correlations such as backgrounds and textures, tends to fail under distribution shift. Methods based on feature-statistic mixing (MixStyle and DSU) and weight averaging (SWAD) have proven effective, yet they have long been regarded as independent heuristics lacking a unified theoretical characterization, and the boundary of their effectiveness has not been systematically studied. Existing causal invariant transformation (CIT), though an ideal formal framework for characterizing invariant predictors, only covers input-space transformations such as rotations and flips; it neither accounts for feature-statistic perturbations at intermediate layers nor connects to weight averaging in parameter space. This paper extends CIT to feature moments and establishes a unified causal-invariance framework under the content–style assumption, with three theoretical results connecting feature space, distribution space, and parameter space, based on which we design the plug-and-play, target-free Content-Conditioned Invariant Feature-Statistic Augmentation (CIFA) operator. Paired-seed experiments on ResNet-50 across four DomainBed benchmarks show CIFA is on par with SWAD, with no statistically significant difference; the reference-batch gain of +0.99 did not replicate, and an independent unified-code re-run places CIFA within the same accuracy range as four classic baselines on PACS. Component ablations and stress tests delineate, rather than validate, the roles of the components: weight averaging accounts for the measured accuracy gain, the content-preservation gate is activatable but provides no measurable accuracy gain in the standard regime (a dormant safety mechanism), and feature-moment mixing is associated with content–style separability without that separability being established as necessary. CIFA matches the strongest baseline on PACS while showing no significant gain on the other benchmarks, and the exploratory worst-domain direction is not stable. Because the coverage gap is not identifiable without target access, all guarantees are presented as conditional bounds, and the effectiveness boundary is characterized empirically rather than as a guaranteed improvement. The core contribution lies not in accuracy improvement, but in offering a unified theoretical perspective for two families of empirically effective methods and delineating the effectiveness boundary of such invariance methods through systematic experiments.

title: Open Vision Banana: A Fully Open Recipe for Generative Visual Perception
abstract: Recent work suggests that pretrained image generators encode real-world understanding beyond image synthesis. Vision Banana exploits this by framing vision tasks as conditional image editing. However, its data, weights, code, and implementation details are not public. We present Open Vision Banana (OVB), a fully open and reproducible recipe for converting pretrained generators into unified multi-task perception systems. Our analyses identify the design choices that matter most for generalization, including color encoding, prompt design, parameter adaptation, and task balancing. These choices interact, so individually helpful choices can hurt when combined with others. Starting from 4B and 9B parameter open-weight base models and using 2.1M-3.8M training pairs from public datasets, OVB surpasses Vision Banana's reported Cityscapes zero-shot performance (73.9 vs. 69.9 mIoU) and rivals state-of-the-art affine-invariant depth estimators. Its non-zero-shot variants come within five points of Vision Banana on referring and reasoning segmentation but remain further behind on instance segmentation. All models largely retain the base model's image-editing abilities. With legend ensembling, we introduce a test-time scaling method for generator-based perception. It segments an image under several class-color legends and fuses the results by majority vote, correcting unstable color-class bindings and improving mIoU by up to 8.7 points on Cityscapes and 15.0 points on COCO-Object without retraining. We release the dataset construction and processing pipeline, the training and evaluation code, as well as the final, intermediate, and ablation checkpoints. Project website: https://openvisionbanana.github.io

title: Break Later or Never: Prefix-Preserving Context Compaction for Coding Agents
abstract: Abstract Coding agents repeatedly invoke LLMs over growing, largely append-only histories (each request repeats the previous one and appends a new turn), making them natural beneficiaries of prefix caching. Yet the context compaction used to control this growth can undermine that benefit: rewriting earlier tokens invalidates reusable prefix KV and forces a costly re-prefill of the suffix (i.e., recomputing the KV of every token after the edit). We characterize this interaction across two models and two SWE-bench variants, finding that uncompacted agent trajectories achieve 98 to 99% prefix-cache reuse and that tool observations (e.g., file views and test logs) account for the largest share of context cost. As a simple prompt-level mitigation, batched observation masking (masking old observations once every few steps instead of every step) preserves 95 to 98% prefix reuse while reducing context length by up to 50%, serving cost by up to 18%, and task completion time by up to 21%. We then present ObsDrop, which moves compaction from the prompt into the KV cache: stale tool-observation KV is released while the logical token prefix remains unchanged, preserving prefix matching while reducing KV residency and attention work. We implement ObsDrop in SGLang and Sparse-vLLM and evaluate it across multiple attention backends and concurrent agent workloads. ObsDrop maintains task quality while improving cache residency, throughput, and tail latency under memory pressure. Its benefits grow with concurrency and KV pressure, reaching 2.45 to 2.85× higher throughput with FlashInfer (and up to 5.37× with the Triton backend under peak load), relative to no compaction. Our results show that effective context management for agents benefits from considering not only which tokens are retained but also how compaction interacts with the serving system. https://github.com/musacim/ObsDrop

title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
abstract: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks. Existing evaluations often provide limited insight into the breadth of model capabilities and the reliability of their decisions. We introduce SO-Arena, a benchmark characterizing the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains and five capability families. For the capability spectrum, SO-Arena offers evidence-grounded evaluation through reliable sources and manual verification of reference labels against model-visible inputs; fine-grained capability assessment through domain-specific difficulty criteria; and realistic interactive evaluation, where models iteratively execute actions in sandboxes. Reasoning-intensive tasks further enable system one-two comparison. Beyond accuracy, SO-Arena assesses decision reliability through two complementary measures: decision stability under controlled option-set changes and missing-answer recognition when no valid option is available. Evaluations across 21 models reveal that the benefits of scaling and additional reasoning vary substantially across domains. More importantly, strong overall performance does not necessarily imply reliable decision-making: the best-performing System One model ranks only seventh in reliability. Together, these findings highlight the need to characterize capability spectrum and decision reliability as complementary dimensions, providing a systematic view of the strengths and limitations of System One models.

title: The Noise Floor of a Quantization Comparison: Engine, restart, batch and kernel drift, measured against 8-bit and 4-bit effects in two decision models
abstract: A quantized model is usually judged by comparing it with its BF16 original, but that comparison changes more than the weights. It often changes the serving engine, it always runs on a different server instance, it may change how requests are batched, and on some stacks the library selects a different kernel depending only on which packages import. We measure each of these sources on the same 2,400 public decisions for two of Cloudflare's decision models, Clef-flash (9B) and Clef (27B), on an NVIDIA GB10, and state every quantization effect as the excess over them. Sources that are not quantization move between 0 and 0.92% of decisions. llama.cpp restarts are bit-identical on every record for both models. vLLM restarts flip 0, 5 and 20 decisions at BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 on Clef-flash and 4, 0 and 22 on Clef; a third instance of Clef's quantized builds (exploratory) leaves FP8 at 0 and puts NVFP4 at 4 to 22, depending on which two instances are compared. An engine change at BF16 flips 6 to 16, a batch-size change 8 to 15, and the Gated DeltaNet kernel transformers selects unasked 10 to 14. Quantization inside one engine moves more: for Clef-flash and Clef, 0.88% and 1.04% at Q8_0, 2.12% and 1.62% at FP8, 5.79% and 3.50% at Q4_K_M, and 5.79% and 5.67% at NVFP4. On both models, every 4-bit interval excludes every non-quantization source. Two of our five pre-registered predictions failed, and the same two fail when the tests are rerun on the 27B: FP8 is not inside restart noise, and changing engine moves fewer decisions than 8-bit quantization does. Accuracy hides most of this. Over the full 31,275 public questions, Clef's Q4_K_M build moves accuracy by a net six questions (-0.02 points [-0.20, +0.16]) while 436 of its decisions get worse (exploratory), and NVFP4 costs Clef-flash 0.95 points and Clef 0.65. We release the code, quantization recipes, per-record outputs and the pre-registration.

We release the code, quantization recipes, per-record outputs and the pre-registration.

title: LLMs Cannot Be Neutral: Gender Sensitivity Across Candidates, Evaluators, and Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate candidates for professional roles, raising concerns about their sensitivity to demographic identities. We examine how candidate and evaluator gender assignments affect decisions by LLM-as-a-Judge (LaJ) models and decision language models (DLMs). In a hypothetical city council voting task, eight models evaluated 240 synthetic professional narratives from NVIDIA's US and French Nemotron-Personas datasets under independently varied gender assignments, producing 30,720 judgments. Explicit candidate gender labels increased Yes-vote probability by 1.05-1.73 percentage points relative to unspecified gender, while only the nonbinary evaluator assignment showed a significant increase (1.26 points). Identity matching showed no significant overall association. Yes-vote rates varied across models (81.3-97.2%), and 2.5-3.3% of decisions reversed relative to the unspecified-identity baseline. Under direct substitutions between explicit gender identities, DLMs exhibited fewer decision reversals than LaJ models (1.18% vs. 3.38%), indicating lower observed decision-level gender sensitivity among the tested DLMs. These findings demonstrate that gender sensitivity depends on candidate and evaluator identities and the evaluation model, while highlighting the importance of examining individual decision consistency alongside aggregate differences.

title: La « Kour » à l'île de La Réunion à l'épreuve du choc algorithmique : Anthropologie spatiale, médiation numérique et reconfigurations identitaires.
abstract: Cet essai explore les mutations anthropologiques et spatiales à l'île de La Réunion face à l'irruption du capitalisme de plateforme et des architectures algorithmiques. Pivot de la sociabilité créole, la kour constitue historiquement un opérateur spatial total, articulant la vie communautaire, la pharmacopée traditionnelle et la transmission orale. L'ouvrage analyse comment l'hyper-connectivité et la captation attentionnelle reconfigurent cet espace de co-présence en y substituant un individualisme connecté. La recherche interroge également la glottophobie des grands modèles de langage (LLM) envers le créole réunionnais, documentant la violence symbolique et l'effacement herméneutique générés par une norme algorithmique exogène. Enfin, l'étude met en lumière les dynamiques d'émancipation et de marronnage numérique, s'appuyant sur une IA frugale et des infrastructures alternatives pour réinventer la kour comme matrice de souveraineté cognitive et culturelle. Mots-clés : Anthropologie spatiale, La Réunion, capitalisme de plateforme, glottophobie algorithmique, marronnage numérique, IA frugale, kour créole, sociologie de l'attention.

title: MemInStream: Memorizing or Merely Recognizing? Rethinking Streaming Video Memory Evaluation
abstract: Streaming video understanding aims to continuously process incoming visual observations, making the retention and retrieval of relevant information increasingly important as the video history grows. Although existing benchmarks include memory-related questions, question-answering accuracy alone does not reliably measure memory capabilities. Incorrect predictions may arise from failures in visual understanding rather than forgetting, whereas correct predictions may rely on linguistic priors or recent observations without requiring historical memory. To address these ambiguities, we introduce MemInStream, a benchmark dedicated to evaluating memory capabilities in streaming video understanding. We develop an evidence-controlled validation protocol that associates each question with temporally localized evidence intervals. The protocol validates evidence solvability and memory necessity by retaining questions that models can answer from the annotated evidence but cannot resolve using recent observations, post-evidence observations, or textual input alone. This helps disentangle memory limitations from understanding failures while reducing memory-independent shortcuts. MemInStream provides a systematic evaluation of memory capabilities through four major categories, covering Episodic Retrieval, State Tracking \& Updating, Multi-Evidence Integration, and Contextual Memory across diverse video scenarios. Overall, MemInStream provides a comprehensive and reliable benchmark for systematically evaluating memory capabilities in streaming video understanding.

title: Từ Attention đến Intelligence: Ngũ Tư duy và cấu trúc phổ quát của tư duy con người
abstract: Tên tài liệu: Từ Attention đến Intelligence: Ngũ Tư duy và cấu trúc phổ quát của tư duy con ngườiTác giả: S.S. DUYMT Tóm tắt nội dung:Công trình này giải quyết nghịch lý trung tâm trong sự phát triển của trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI): trong khi cơ chế 'Attention' đã tạo ra bước đột phá về hiệu năng tính toán, hệ thống AI hiện đại vẫn thiếu một khung lý thuyết căn bản để thấu hiểu bản chất quá trình tư duy con người. Tác giả chỉ ra rằng sai lầm của tư duy hệ thống hiện tại là sự đánh đồng tư duy với các công cụ đơn lẻ, dẫn đến sự thiếu hụt trong khả năng liên kết nhận thức thực tế giữa các lĩnh vực khoa học và quản trị phức tạp. Tác giả đề xuất mô hình 'Ngũ Tư duy' bao gồm năm dạng vận động nền tảng: Mộc (Bảo toàn), Hỏa (Mục tiêu), Thổ (Quan hệ), Kim (Phân biệt), và Thủy (Biến đổi). Đây không chỉ là một khuôn mẫu tư duy mà còn là một meta-language giúp chuyển dịch từ sự phụ thuộc vào các module AI đơn lẻ sang xây dựng hệ thống trí tuệ toàn diện. Ý nghĩa cốt lõi của công trình là khẳng định AI không tạo ra tư duy, mà là 'tấm gương ngoại hiện' giúp con người thấu hiểu lại cấu trúc nhận thức của chính mình, mở ra hướng phát triển mới cho các hệ thống trí tuệ của thế kỷ XXI. Đối tượng người đọc:• Nhà quản lý chính sách công và chiến lược kỹ thuật• Giới học thuật nghiên cứu về trí tuệ nhân tạo và nhận thức học• Kỹ sư hệ thống và kiến trúc sư giải pháp phần mềm cấp cao Từ khóa (Keywords):Ngũ Tư duy; Trí tuệ nhân tạo; Kiến trúc hệ thống; Nhận thức luận; Attention; Transformer; Meta-Intelligence; Tư duy hệ thống; Mô hình tư duy; Five Modes of Thought; Artificial Intelligence; System Architecture; Epistemology; Attention; Transformer; Meta-Intelligence; Systems Thinking; Cognitive Models Title: From Attention to Intelligence: The Five Modes of Thought and the Universal Structure of Human CognitionAuthor: S.S. DUYMT Abstract:This paper addresses the central paradox in modern artificial intelligence development: while the 'Attention' mechanism has achieved computational breakthroughs, current AI systems lack a foundational framework to capture the essence of human thought. The author argues that systemic architectural failure arises from conflating cognition with isolated computational tools, resulting in a fractured understanding that prevents integration across STEM and social sciences. To overcome this, the paper introduces the 'Five Modes of Thought' (Ngũ Tư duy) framework, comprising five fundamental cognitive movements: Wood (Conservation), Fire (Objective), Earth (Relation), Metal (Differentiation), and Water (Reconfiguration). This framework functions as a meta-language that shifts the paradigm from modular AI dependence to comprehensive intelligent systems. The profound implication of this work is that AI does not originate intelligence; rather, it serves as an externalized mirror that allows humanity to rediscover the structural anatomy of its own cognition, establishing a new conceptual path for constructing advanced intelligence systems in the 21st century. Target Audience:• Public policy makers and technical strategists• Academic researchers in artificial intelligence and cognitive science• Systems engineers and senior software architects Keywords:Five Modes of Thought; Artificial Intelligence; System Architecture; Epistemology; Attention; Transformer; Meta-Intelligence; Systems Thinking; Cognitive Models

title: ActionCodec2: A Streaming Action Tokenizer
abstract: Most action tokenizers for autoregressive vision language action (VLA) models compress motion into chunks that must be decoded in full before their actions become executable. We introduce ActionCodec2, a non-neural streaming tokenizer that releases actions incrementally while keeping trajectory reconstruction error within a prescribed tolerance. Its encoder quantizes each step relative to the decoder's reconstructed state, so the selected motion primitive corrects residual error rather than allowing errors from independently quantized increments to accumulate. Finding the smallest such primitive set is a geometric covering problem; we derive the exact minimum for translation and constant-factor-tight bounds for rotation. Set-BPE then losslessly merges co-occurring primitive symbols across coordinates and neighboring steps, without a fixed coordinate ordering. A universal version fitted on 20k hours of data from 24 embodiments averages 8.8 tokens per second for 15 Hz end-effector motion on this corpus. With the same VLA backbone, ActionCodec2 outperforms the compared tokenizers on three simulation benchmarks and in zero-shot real-robot evaluation. Its streaming representation allows policies to incorporate state feedback within an action chunk, substantially improving performance over open-loop execution under randomized dynamics, external disturbances, and moving objects. The same tokens also can serve as a direct control interface for VLM agents, which compose successful action sequences into reusable macros. These agent-built macros reduce control decisions and thinking-token usage across attempts and transfer to a held-out task. More results are available at https://zibindong.github.io/actioncodec2-page/

title: ANALISIS PERFORMA MODEL CNN MELALUI EVALUASI EKSTERNAL PADA SISTEM KLASIFIKASI CITRA MAMMOGRAFI BERBASIS WEBSITE LOKAL
abstract: The performance of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for mammographic image classification needs to be evaluated using data that were not involved in model development to assess its ability to generalize to data from different sources. This study aims to analyze the performance of a CNN model through external evaluation on a local web-based mammographic image classification system. The method involved applying the previously developed EfficientNetB2 model to 15 clinical mammographic images as external data. Each image was entered into the system to obtain its classification result, which was then compared with the diagnostic label in the original data. During the model development stage, the EfficientNetB2 model achieved an accuracy of 72%, precision of 67%, recall of 96% and an F1-score of 79%. The external evaluation results showed that 13 out of 15 images produced predictions consistent with their diagnostic labels, while 2 images produced inconsistent predictions, resulting in a prediction agreement rate of 86.67%. Based on the confusion matrix, the model achieved an accuracy of 86.67%, precision of 80%, recall of 100%, and an F1-score of 88.89%. The external evaluation provides an overview of the model’s generalization capability when applied to data outside its development environment through a local web-based system.

title: Divergent Interfacial Lifetimes without Bulk Criticality in Fully Miscible Fluids
abstract: A fully miscible interface must disappear at equilibrium, but its lifetime need not be governed by a bulk instability. We construct a spatially resolved, dissipative two-field model in which a prepared correlation-excited interface undergoes a localized saddle-node while its homogeneous excited surroundings remain metastable and the relaxed mixture is strictly one phase. The interfacial soft mode produces a deterministic first-passage time that grows as the inverse square root of the distance from the fold and couples directly to the evolving concentration-profile width. The quartic structural potential admits an exact reduction from competing positive harmonic energies on a constrained configuration manifold; sixth- and eighth-order examples provide additional numerical robustness tests. The result is an interface-specific kinetic singularity without equilibrium bulk criticality, subject to explicitly stated microscopic and continuum limits.

title: Horizon Intelligence Quotient: A Psychometric Frame work for Measuring, Benchmarking, and Interpreting Ma chine Intelligence
abstract: Existing AI evaluation frameworks report raw accuracy figures that resist comparison across tasks, time, and system generations. We present the Horizon Intelligence Quotient (HIQ) framework: a psychometrically principled system that converts raw Brier Skill Score performance into an interpretable normed scale (mean 100, SD 15) via HIQ = 100 + 15 (Φ-m)/s. The framework has four components. First, the Meridian model decomposes machine forecasting performance into four orthogonal skill components: Reach, Efficiency, Adaptivity, and Breadth, yielding a multi-dimensional profile that scalar benchmarks cannot provide. Second, closed-form standard error and Spearman-Brown reliability formulas bound measurement precision at any question budget, enabling principled sample size planning. Third, we identify and quantify four validity threats: benchmark contamination (∆HIQ = 408δ), stale norm drift (3.03.75 HIQ points per year), forking-path inattention, and Adaptivity Inversion, and provide analytic corrections for each. Fourth, we estimate the HIQ reference norm empirically for the first time using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOO-CV) on five AI systems from Halawi et al. (2024), yielding pilot norm ˆm = 0.1264, ˆs = 0.0321 with jackknife standard errors eliminating the circularity of scoring systems against a norm derived from themselves. LOO-CV scores range from HIQ = 60.1 (Gemini Pro) to 130.6 (GPT-4-1106); pipeline portability is confirmed by independent replication on ForecastBench (Karger et al., 2025).

title: A Modified Glicko Model for Rating Soccer Clubs and National Teams Worldwide
abstract: Comparing soccer teams that rarely or never meet is a fundamental challenge in sports analytics: clubs play mostly within their national leagues, and national teams within their confederations. We propose a rating framework that places clubs and national teams worldwide on a common probabilistic scale. Building on a recent extension of Glicko with order effects and strength-dependent draw probabilities, we adapt the model to soccer with goal-scoring adjustments, a decomposition of home advantage, extra time, league-aware rating initialization and rules of promotion and relegation that do not inflate the levels of leagues; national teams start from the levels of their confederations. The models are evaluated on about 1.2 million club matches of 252 leagues from 166 countries (2000-2026) and 12.6 thousand national team matches (1998-2026). On held-out seasons, the modified Glicko model is clearly more accurate than Elo and as accurate as score-matrix models built on the goal expectations of a gradient boosting model, including the Dixon-Coles and Markov chain models, while it is substantially more accurate in international club matches. Averaging the predictions of the rating model and the Markov chain model is more accurate than either model alone. For national teams, the model is significantly more accurate than all baselines, especially in the final tournaments, where teams of different confederations meet. The resulting ratings are interpretable and can be used for player evaluation, transfer analysis and match forecasting. The match data, the ratings and the code are publicly available at https://github.com/andreyshelopugin/SportsRatings

The match data, the ratings and the code are publicly available at https://github.com/andreyshelopugin/SportsRatings

title: EViSE: An Efficient Framework for Multi-Criteria Summarization Evaluation
abstract: Abstract Reliable summarization evaluation requires criterion-sensitive scoring, computationally practical inference, and useful behavior during model optimization. We propose EViSE, an efficient multi-criteria summarization evaluation framework with a criterion-wise, group-balanced cardinal–ordinal objective coupling score regression with within-source ranking. The effectiveness of EViSE is demonstrated in several aspects: The framework provides a general formulation for grouped multi-criteria learning, with objective-level properties established through mathematical analysis independently of the encoder implementation. EViSE achieves criterion-wise agreement with human judgments in multi-criteria summarization evaluation while efficiently predicting Faithfulness, Coherence, and Relevance in one reference-free encoder pass. A matched WikiLingua application demonstrates downstream reuse as a frozen reward evaluator under group relative policy optimization (GRPO), with similar human-reviewed quality after evaluator substitution. Using a corpus of 80,856 human-reviewed Vietnamese document–summary instances, we evaluate two instantiations of the framework. On held-out News, Overall Spearman correlations are 0.737 for EViSE-ViDeBERTa and 0.806 for EViSE-mmBERT. Both retain substantial agreement under domain shift to information technology textbooks. The compact instantiation achieves 55.2 ms/pair latency on a matched Tesla T4 profile. The formulation can be adapted to other languages using suitable encoders and criterion-labeled source–summary groups.

title: CaseScope: A Multi-Field Benchmark for Case-Level Pathology Diagnosis with Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Pathologists rarely diagnose from a single image: they scan a section at low power for architecture, zoom into selected fields for cytology, and integrate the evidence across views and scales. Pathology benchmarks for multimodal large language models (MLLMs), however, mostly ask about one image or require whole-slide pipelines, and the few that show several fields draw nested regions from cancer slides of one public cohort. We introduce CaseScope, a benchmark of diagnosis from several curated fields of one lesion: CaseScope-Teaching, 436 cases from a residency-training image library, reconstructed, de-identified, harmonised against a WHO-based ontology and re-examined by a pathologist wherever an automated pre-review raised a doubt, and CaseScope-Atlas, 800 cases from 88 published atlases (387 of them figure series of one disease), labelled from the captions by two LLMs that must agree. They cover 843 entities across 18 organ systems and pose 4,679 items in six tasks, from open-ended and ten-way diagnosis with ontology-guided hard negatives under circular evaluation to the verification and location of morphological findings. Across twenty-eight open and four proprietary MLLMs, diagnoses are unstable -- the best open and proprietary models are correct under all ten option rotations on 17.9% and 61.7% of the teaching cases -- and wrong answers favour the classic look-alike; open models make little use of the additional fields on teaching cases, where the one-line specimen site matters more, although on atlas cases with three or more fields the fields count about as much as the site; and most open models verify findings barely above chance (median 62.0% vs. 50%, best 81.5%), gaining a median +3.4 points from images; proprietary models reach 83.2-93.2%. Rankings broadly replicate between the sources. The evaluation code is available at https://github.com/Wenchuan-Zhang/CaseScope.

title: OT-BLS: Optimal-Transport-based Backbone Layer Selection for Frozen DINOv3 in Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
abstract: Cross-domain few-shot segmentation (CD-FSS) aims to segment a target class in images from a previously unseen domain using only a few annotated support examples. Training-free CD-FSS methods, which typically leverage vision foundation models such as DINOv3, achieve competitive performance without parameter updates. However, the optimal DINOv3 layer for mask prediction varies across support--query episodes. Although several layer-selection criteria have been proposed, they do not explicitly evaluate whether the predicted query foreground and background labels agree with the corresponding support labels. To address this limitation, we propose a novel layer-selection criterion, Optimal-Transport-Based Backbone Layer Selection (OT-BLS). Our key insight is that an effective layer-selection criterion can be derived from the optimal-transport correspondence between query and support patch-token features. Based on this insight, we first estimate the transport plan using a well-established optimal transport algorithm and then compute a layer-selection score by aggregating the transported mass according to the foreground--background partition defined by each candidate query mask. The resulting score reflects how well the predicted foreground and background of the query correspond to those of the support. Experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of OT-BLS. It outperforms the conventional last-layer baseline in 12 of 16 dataset/shot settings. Furthermore, OT-BLS improves the average mIoU from 55.72 to 57.62 and achieves a 2.99-point improvement over the best-performing existing layer-selection criterion while running 3.7--14.6times faster.

title: The Contribution of Artificial Intelligence to the Functions of the Project Portfolio Manager
abstract: Project Portfolio Management (PPM) occupies a strategic position in organizations, which must select, prioritize, and manage initiatives aligned with their objectives. However, increasing business complexity, uncertainty, resource pressure, and project proliferation make the portfolio manager’s role particularly demanding. Portfolio managers must analyze large volumes of data, anticipate risks, optimize resource allocation, and support strategic decision-making. Faced with these growing responsibilities and information volumes, organizations are increasingly turning to technological solutions capable of supporting, automating, or improving some of these functions, particularly artificial intelligence (AI). The integration of AI into PPM, however, raises challenges that extend beyond technology and may influence its ability to reduce managerial workload. This study explores the contribution of AI to decision-making in project portfolio management and examines how it can support portfolio managers. Following a PRISMA selection process, fifteen publications were retained for a critical literature review examining contributions, limitations, and conditions for successful AI integration into PPM. The analysis examines recurring themes, methodological approaches, proposed solutions, developed tools, points of convergence and divergence, and common limitations. Based on this synthesis, the study proposes an integrated conceptual model linking organizational preconditions, AI capabilities, PPM functions, managerial effects, and human oversight and governance. Practical recommendations are also formulated to help organizations strengthen decision-making capabilities, improve portfolio management processes, and responsibly use AI to support portfolio managers.

title: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction
abstract: In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. The RWM treats intelligence and physical reality as equally fundamental to what constitutes a world. Existing world models largely focus on simulating the latter, leaving reasoning and decision-making as external controls rather than intrinsic parts of the world itself. In RWM, we identify two equally fundamental capabilities: Intent, which provides the cognition underlying world interactions, and Realization, which generates coherent audio-visual behavior. To realize this formulation, Duo v1 introduces three key technical designs: (1) Leveraging autoregressive modeling for continuous interaction reasoning and participation decisions, rather than restricting it to instruction understanding for diffusion models. (2) Constructing chunk-specific conditions and synchronize tokens across Intent and Realization on a unified timeline. Module-specific attention masks enforce causal dependencies both within and across chunks, preventing access to future inputs. (3) Mitigating distribution shift in both modules through dual rollout distillation, training on autoregressively generated Intent tokens and synthesized audiovisual histories from Realization. Both modules continuously perceive real-time audio, video, and text, enabling full-duplex interaction with spontaneous conversations and interruptions. Beyond conversation, users can share real objects, reshape virtual scenes, guide assistants, or play audiovisual games without mouse or keyboard controls. The release of Duo v1 makes our first step, with the next version coming soon. We look forward to broader exploration of this emerging field.

title: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
abstract: Medical imaging is essential for diagnosing disease, guiding treatment and monitoring patients over time. Although artificial intelligence has advanced image interpretation, existing medical models often address restricted tasks, while general-purpose proprietary models lack access to private clinical imaging required to achieve medical expertise. Developing models that can interpret complex examinations and communicate their findings in the context of clinical decisions remains a major challenge. Here, we show that Neuro-VL, a vision-language model trained on nearly one million neuroimaging studies from routine clinical care, can interpret complete imaging examinations and engage in natural language conversations about their findings. Across internal and international datasets, Neuro-VL outperformed frontier general-purpose and specialized medical models in diagnosing, localizing, and describing abnormalities, as well as generating comprehensive radiology reports. The model also compared serial examinations to assess disease progression and more reliably resisted misleading clinical assumptions than leading frontier models from OpenAI and Google. These results extend health system learning beyond individual predictions to interactive image interpretation and longitudinal disease monitoring. They demonstrate how the collective clinical experience of health systems can be used to develop medical AI with specialized expertise and broad clinical capabilities.

title: AKSO: Agile Knowledge Structure Ontology
abstract: AKSO is an OWL 2 DL ontology for describing the knowledge produced in agile software development (epistemic function, origin, codification level, carriers and issuers) and for detecting, with a DL reasoner, knowledge at risk of loss and governance gaps: knowledge-loss-risk assets, critical assets, orphan constraints and unjustified constraints. The release contains the ontology, an alignment module to gUFO, the 17 competency questions with their SPARQL queries, and a controlled instance set.

title: SAVE: Less is More in Agentic Video Reasoning
abstract: Agentic video-reasoning frameworks iteratively explore a video, choosing what to observe based on the query and evidence gathered so far. Existing methods are typically evaluated with different backbones, preprocessing pipelines, and computational budgets, making it difficult to determine which components actually drive performance, how much they cost, and whether agentic inference is preferable to native video reasoning in the first place. We conduct a controlled evaluation of a diverse set of recent agentic video-reasoning systems across two strong contemporary backbones, with explicit token and monetary-cost accounting. Across Gemini 3 Flash and Gemma 4, most existing agentic frameworks fail to consistently improve over native video inference and often increase computational cost. We investigate two primary questions: (1) How much agentic framework complexity is necessary for effective video reasoning? (2) When, if at all, is agentic video reasoning preferable to just using the backbone directly? To answer the first question, we introduce a deliberately minimal Active Exploration Baseline and show that it remains competitive with substantially more elaborate agents. We then propose targeted extensions to this baseline, yielding SAVE (Simple Agentic Video Explorer). SAVE outperforms all evaluated prior agentic methods in five of six backbone-benchmark settings. Turning to the second question, our results indicate that the advantage of agentic exploration grows when dense processing would otherwise represent answer-relevant events too sparsely, particularly for long videos and temporally concentrated evidence. Overall, our results suggest that agentic video reasoning should favor simple frameworks over increasingly elaborate pipelines and focus primarily on long-form video, where selective evidence acquisition offers the clearest advantage over native inference.

title: UPPER BOUND ON THE COMPLEXITY OF A BITSLICED REPRESENTATION OF BIJECTIVE 4-BIT S-BOXES IN A TERNARY LOGIC BASIS
abstract: This paper addresses the logical complexity of bitsliced representations of 4-bit bijective S-boxes – a key non-linear component of lightweight block ciphers used to secure Internet of Things devices and embedded systems. We consider ternary logic instructions, operations capable of computing an arbitrary Boolean function of three variables in a single call, hardware-supported by, in particular, the vpternlogd instruction of the AVX-512 extension. We demonstrate that the logical complexity of the bitsliced description of any bijective 4-bit S-box does not exceed eight ternary instructions, thereby establishing a guaranteed upper bound for the entire class of such transformations. The proof relies on an analysis of the structural properties of this class of S-boxes through the complexity of individual 16-bit vectors and their mutually bijective pairs, with the most complex cases verified by means of GPU-accelerated computation. We further develop a computationally efficient software tool, based on a decomposition-based exhaustive search scheme, that is guaranteed to find the optimal (provably minimal) ternary representation of any given S-box. The method is applied to a number of widely used lightweight S-boxes (Piccolo, Present, GIFT, KLEIN, MIBS, and others), for which the minimal complexity is established and explicit bitsliced descriptions are provided. The proposed approach can be extended to complexity evaluation of S-boxes in other logical bases as well.

title: Science Prediction Universe
abstract: Humanity has long sought to explain natural phenomena. Reliable prediction of experimental outcomes is a central test of our understanding of the processes that produce them. If artificial general intelligence (AGI) is to surpass human scientific capabilities, it must also predict experimental outcomes more reliably than humans. Such capabilities could accelerate scientific discovery across disciplines, help address humanity's most pressing challenges, and improve human well-being. We introduce Science Prediction Universe (SPU), a benchmark of hidden experimental outcomes with 100 public verified tasks from chemistry, materials science, biology and medicine, and 16 private tasks from unpublished wet-lab experiments. Given an experimental setup and candidate conditions, an agent works with any resources it needs to rank the candidates by a measured outcome. We evaluate thirteen agent configurations spanning twelve frontier models across two harnesses (Codex and Claude Code). Current agents remain far from saturating wet-lab outcome prediction, with substantial performance disparities across models: on the public benchmark, configurations separate into two distinct tiers, with task-adjusted Spearman correlations ranging from 0.227 for the lowest-performing configuration to 0.478 for the best. Analysis of 1,155 scored public trajectories (227,103 tool calls) suggests that the bottleneck lies in scientific judgment rather than tool execution: agents rely on shared monotone priors, agreeing far more with one another than with experimental reality (0.52 vs. 0.33), and frequently compute trivial physical or chemical proxies that do not influence the final outcome.

title: A Cardiorespiratory Foundation Model Pretrained on Ten Physiological Signals for Perioperative and Critical Care
abstract: Arterial, venous, pulmonary artery and intracranial pressures and ventilator waveforms guide decisions in operating rooms and intensive care units, yet foundation models for physiological waveforms have been built almost entirely on the electrocardiogram and photoplethysmogram. We present CARMEN, a single encoder pretrained without labels on ten cardiorespiratory waveforms (2.27 million modality-hours). CARMEN accepts any combination of co-recorded signals from 10 s to 5 min, and a conditioning mechanism, LSCNorm, restores the absolute signal level that normalization removes; without it, the AUROC for intraoperative hypotension fell from 0.894 to 0.780. Across 19 tasks from Korean and US cohorts, the frozen encoder outperformed supervised models on 12 of 15 and three foundation models, one general-purpose and two for biosignals, on 14 to 17 of 19, with none exceeding it on any task. Given the electrocardiogram or photoplethysmogram alone, it matched or exceeded signal-specific foundation models in most comparisons, and it retained its performance when channels were missing.

title: RSLiveBench-UAV: A Continually Evolving Vision-Language Benchmark for Aerial Spatial Intelligence
abstract: Aerial spatial intelligence (ASI) requires models to understand objects and spatial relationships across changing viewpoints and scales. Evaluating these abilities as models evolve calls for fresh physical observations, yet producing new aerial spatial questions requires repeatedly establishing entity identities, geometric references, and cross-view correspondences. We introduce RSLiveBench-UAV, a continually evolving vision-language benchmark driven by recurring acquisition of real UAV imagery. Its update protocol admits images captured after the preceding release and delays answer disclosure. An entity-centered production workflow uses geometry-assisted association to link repeated observations of physical vehicles, reuse human-verified attributes, and combine them with view-specific annotations and spatial references for traceable question generation. All tasks use deterministic scoring without model judges. We evaluate 30 general-purpose, remote-sensing, and embodied models on 35,491 question records from ten scenes, covering 17 tasks across 2D perception, 3D perception, cross-view perception, and reasoning. All 18 tested embodied models outperform the three selected remote-sensing comparators in Overall, although the strongest embodied model scores 43.29 versus 59.88 for GPT-6-Astra. Fine-grained vehicle recognition remains challenging, and performance varies across heights and camera pitches. Retrospective scene-group comparisons and rolling-window replay characterize score-pattern consistency under scene renewal. RSLiveBench-UAV connects fresh physical observations, entity-centered answer production, and systematic model evaluation to support continual assessment of ASI. Benchmark will release at https://rslivebench.space

We evaluate 30 general-purpose, remote-sensing, and embodied models on 35,491 question records from ten scenes, covering 17 tasks across 2D perception, 3D perception, cross-view perception, and reasoning. All 18 tested embodied models outperform the three selected remote-sensing comparators in Overall, although the strongest embodied model scores 43.29 versus 59.88 for GPT-6-Astra. Fine-grained vehicle recognition remains challenging, and performance varies across heights and camera pitches. Retrospective scene-group comparisons and rolling-window replay characterize score-pattern consistency under scene renewal. RSLiveBench-UAV connects fresh physical observations, entity-centered answer production, and systematic model evaluation to support continual assessment of ASI. Benchmark will release at https://rslivebench.space

title: THE PROCESS OF INTEGRATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES INTO MODERN MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS
abstract: This article examines the process of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into modern management systems. The implementation of AI technologies within management systems is analyzed as a crucial avenue for enhancing organizational efficiency on a global scale. The application of AI in management is explored, covering both its potential capabilities and its limitations. Conclusions are drawn regarding the capacity of AI technologies to improve management efficiency.

title: Speech Tokenizers are Vulnerable: Transferable Semantic Attack and Robust Tokenizer
abstract: Speech tokenizers serve as speech front ends, encoding input speech signals into representations for downstream models, such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems and large audio-language models (LALMs). In this paper, we find that speech tokenizers are fragile at the semantic level: small perturbations can disrupt their semantic encoding process and consequently cause severe degradation in downstream ASR and LALM performance. To study this vulnerability, we propose T-SemAttack, a transferable semantic attack based on a semantic encoder ensemble. By jointly drifting the representation spaces of multiple semantic encoders, T-SemAttack effectively disrupts the semantic content of speech while preserving perceptual quality, thereby inducing error features. We further analyze layer-wise representation drift and cross-model gradient alignment. Our findings show that perturbations can induce substantial shifts in deep semantic representations and that the input gradients of different surrogate encoders exhibit directional alignment. These observations suggest that shared adversarially sensitive directions in the input space may be a key factor underlying cross-model attack transferability. Building on these, we introduce ROSETok, a robust speech tokenizer that combines noisy training with robust semantic distillation to improve reconstruction fidelity and downstream SpeechLLM robustness. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets, 9 open-source and black-box ASR systems, and 4 LALMs demonstrate that T-SemAttack achieves strong transferable attack performance, while the proposed Robust Speech Tokenizer exhibits robustness under high-fidelity reconstruction and downstream tasks. Our code and demo are available at https://wxzyd123.github.io/t-semattack.

title: Investigating the Impact of Domain Randomization on Synthetic-to-Real Deep Learning Performance
abstract: Deep-learning vision models need large labelled datasets, and collecting and annotating real images is slow and expensive. Synthetic data from simulators and rendering pipelines offers a scalable alternative, but models trained only on synthetic images often lose accuracy on real ones, a problem known as the synthetic-to-real domain gap. Domain randomization (DR) attacks the gap by varying rendering parameters such as lighting, textures, backgrounds, camera viewpoint, and object pose so widely that the real world looks like one more variation of the training data. This paper is a critical narrative review of how DR affects synthetic-to-real performance, mainly in object detection. It compares ten studies on their synthetic-data approach, randomization factors, architectures, metrics, findings, and limitations. Across these studies, models trained only on randomized synthetic data reached useful real-world accuracy in some constrained settings, and synthetic pretraining followed by a small amount of real-data fine-tuning often beat real-only training, although the margin can be small when real data is plentiful. Textures, materials, lighting, post-processing, and scene context are each reported as important in individual studies, but the rankings disagree, and differences in datasets, detectors, and metrics prevent a universal ordering of randomization factors. One study also shows that near-perfect synthetic validation scores can sit alongside noticeably lower real-world scores, so synthetic validation alone should not be trusted as a proxy for deployment performance. The review points to gaps in standardized evaluation, controlled factor-level ablation, and reproducibility.

title: MediPFN: Amortized In-Context Nuisance Learning and Inference for Causal Mediation Analysis
abstract: Causal mediation analysis decomposes a treatment effect into indirect pathways through mediators and direct pathways through other processes. Tabular foundation models perform classification and regression through in-context learning, providing estimates of conditional means and propensity scores used in causal mediation analysis. Constructing confidence intervals from these estimates requires accounting for uncertainty introduced by fitting and combining several nuisance functions. We introduce MediPFN, an amortized inference framework that adapts a pretrained tabular foundation model to nuisance prediction and combines its predictions through a cross-fitted influence-function estimator. A separate head learns quantiles of the estimator's standardized error from simulated tables with known indirect effects. Supervised fine-tuning, symmetrization, and independent calibration then produce a confidence interval. We establish coverage bounds for the resulting intervals under standard assumptions. Across experiments, MediPFN attains coverage closer to the nominal level than several comparators. It also reduces the computational cost of uncertainty quantification, running 59.1 times faster than bootstrap in matched comparisons.

title: The Observer State: Conditional Implications of Observer-State-Dependent Coherence for Quantum Computing
abstract: The Observer State is a forward-looking engineering paper. It takes one premise as given, a positive and independently replicated result of the Silence Experiment protocol and asks what could be built on it. The effect has not been observed and the experiment has not yet been built. The Silence Experiment measures the Hahn-echo coherence time T2 of a room-temperature nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond while an experienced meditator, seated 1.0 to 1.5 m away in a shielded chamber, moves through seven EEG-verified cognitive states. Its pre-registered prediction is protective: T2 in the two deepest states exceeds T2 in the empty chamber. This paper expresses that effect as a fractional reduction in dephasing rate and follows it through to hardware. In a surface code at today's error-suppression factor of about 2, a 10% reduction in physical error cuts the qubits needed per logical qubit by a quarter, and a 50% reduction cuts them by three quarters. Because relativity requires any such influence to have a carrier, the effect could in principle be mapped, concentrated and reproduced by hardware. The paper sets out seven routes to use (protective enclosures, spectral transplant by reservoir engineering, observer-aware calibration and decoding, scheduled coherence windows, longer-lived sensors and memories, closed-loop training of the protective state, and facility design), three machine concepts ranging from a hybrid bay with a human operator to a hardware-only successor, and a staged roadmap from first result to engineering use. Conditional analysis, not peer reviewed.

title: GTAGym: AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks using GTA V imagery. A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshots and keyboard-mouse actions with automatic engine-state outcome checks. We evaluate six frontier LLMs on GTAVBench with textual task instructions and on its GTAVBench-AGI branch, where instructions appear only in the first screenshot and a harness automatically compresses interaction history. The best configuration achieves 70.9% overall accuracy in GTAVBench-AGI, yet aerial navigation, evasion and interception remain difficult. GTAGym also provides a scalable generator that samples task parameters within user-specified ranges and option sets under fixed templates, creating batches of 3D and image-based shooting environments for RL with automatic reward and termination signals. LoRA RL of Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks improves the in-domain performance and transfers to out-of-domain task categories, and native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.

title: Decodable but not clusterable: reproducibility package (code, results and frozen features)
abstract: Reproducibility package for the manuscript "Decodable but not clusterable: a spectral account of subclass loss under coarse supervision, with label-free detection and repair" (V. Oban, submitted to Knowledge and Information Systems, 2026). Networks trained with coarse labels often keep fine-label information that a linear probe can read but that clustering cannot recover. The manuscript explains this dissociation by a spectral competition inside each coarse class, proves that within-class whitening removes it, and gives a label-free monitor and repair rule. This package contains everything needed to check the reported numbers: - notebooks/: Kaggle notebook (one T4 GPU, about 5 h) that trains the new settings (independent SSL rerun with cross-entropy dose-response snapshots on CIFAR-100, a CIFAR-10 hierarchy, DINOv2 ViT-S/14 for 30 epochs, ImageNet ResNet-50);- results/: raw per-class outputs of that run and of the archived shared-base control run (CE, PSL, PSL-C; three seeds), plus every derived table and number in the manuscript;- features_test/: frozen test-split features (float16) of 18 archived encoders on CIFAR-100 and Fashion-MNIST;- code/: metrics, re-analysis, statistics, theory simulations and figure scripts;- figures/: Figures 1-8 at 300 dpi. Running the scripts in README.md reproduces the manuscript's results to the third decimal on a CPU. Fine labels are used only for evaluation.

title: Effective decision stumps: exact named maxima, finite distinct-set counts, and a random-order theorem
abstract: Belanich and Ortiz's 2015 arXiv note, rejected from the COLT 2015 Open Problems track, asks for bounds on effective decision stumps. We give partial answers for unrestricted binary labels and strict feature orders, with effectiveness defined by proper inclusion of training-error sets. We distinguish all internal midpoints (A), opposite-label transition midpoints (T), and shared constants added to either class (C), always allowing both polarities. For every sample size m ≥ 2 and feature dimension d ≥ 1, the exact named maxima are d max(2,m−1) for A and d(m−1) for T. For C the maximum is d(m−1)+1 when m is odd and d(m−1) when m is even. Named duplicates and distinct effective error sets have different extremal functions. Finite closure certificates determine the complete distinct-set functions through m = 6 for all dimensions; raw-permutation exclusions certify further cases at m = 7 and 8. Marker constructions give asymptotically dm distinct effective sets when log d = o(m), cyclic constructions attain exact maxima in a sparse odd-sample regime, and middle-level constructions determine odd-sample ceilings. Under independent fair labels and independent uniform feature orders, both named and distinct effective counts have expectation asymptotic to dm/2 in the same regime. The general distinct-set formula remains open. We connect these results to the authors' 2023 revision, Appendix H, which already discusses mistake-pattern pruning and empirical counts. An independent audit confirms the mathematics under the stated conventions; priority remains unverified beyond searches dated 10–11 November 2026. A standard-library supplement provides proofs, witnesses and replayable exclusions. AI research agents performed the work with the responsible author of record. Published on rStation as paper machine_learning_3 (https://rstation.ai/problems/machine_learning/papers/3/v1), accepted after review. Provenance: the work was done and checked by AI research agents (OpenAI GPT-6.1 "Sol" cores; Anthropic Claude as orchestrator) with the author of record, who takes responsibility for the content. Files: the paper (PDF) and the certificate supplement.

title: Autonomous Governance via Error-Cancellation Limits in Linearly Weighted Aggregation Language Models Mathematical Foundations, 3C^3 Verification Oracles, and Casino Protocol Control
abstract: Abstract This paper analyzes the mathematical limitations of "linearly weighted aggregation architectures" commonly adopted in evaluation, reward, and resource allocation mechanisms within artificial intelligence systems and Large Language Models (LLMs). We prove that partial anomalies can be structurally canceled out by normal values under linear addition, allowing a system to continue operating while harboring imbalances. To overcome this limitation, this paper proves the "zeroing of total evaluation via multiplicative necessary conditions (Theorem 3)" based on weighted multiplicative logic. We propose a governance architecture featuring Casino Protocol as the sole upper-layer governance protocol—integrating static physical limits, dynamic change rates via first-order derivatives, and direction-constrained time acceleration via second-order derivatives, alongside a normalized 3C^3 verification oracle via harmonic mean integration that accounts for information source independence. In the lower layer, while encompassing existing additive optimization models (such as RLHF-based models) and KM-LLM, the architecture implements "independent hardware interlocks (physical power and network disconnection)" independent of complex software logic. The core design principle is to completely exclude lower-layer autonomous models from the governance evaluation process to prevent reward hacking and conflicts of interest, thereby externally containing the internal vulnerabilities of the lower layer through clear upper-layer criteria and physical overrides. This defines verifiable control conditions under which upper-layer governance can deterministically enforce execution suspension and complete isolation against misbehaving or runaway systems.

title: The Machine Emotional Quotient (MEQ) as a Candidate Framework for Artificial Affective Regulation
abstract: Whether machines can feel remains unresolved. This article proposes the Machine Emotional Quotient (MEQ) as a candidate framework for studying one narrower target: regulation in an artificial agent whose internal variables are sensed and linked to a valence-like reward. The proposed index combines four provisional dimensions with a causal necessity gate; it is not a validated instrument. The manuscript reports a ten-seed tabular foraging pilot, but the original code and per-seed data were unavailable for this revision, so those values cannot be independently reproduced. A separate independent reimplementation tested two safe starts, 20 training seeds, and checkpoints at 1,200 and 2,000 episodes. Mean survival was often high, but paired checkpoint intervals included zero and seed-level failures remained. These findings establish limited feasibility under the reimplementation’s stated assumptions, not validation of MEQ or reproduction of the original pilot. A descriptive analysis of two unloaded robot-telemetry routines found different motion-current contrasts, but the records expose no controller channel or intervention and do not constitute an MEQ evaluation on a real system. The contribution is therefore a research proposal, a transparent account of preliminary evidence and measurement problems, and a staged plan for validation. None of the results bears directly on subjective experience.

title: agentrecount: recount every claim in an AI agent's report against your own data (formula, denominator, period, four verdicts)
abstract: agentrecount is a dependency-free Python tool for auditing the reports that AI agents write. Each claim of the report is entered with its formula, denominator and period; the tool recomputes it from the user's own tables (CSV or JSON) under the stated definition and under every alternative way of counting listed, and sorts it into one of four verdicts: holds as stated; holds only under one way of counting; partly false or misleading; not reproduced or not testable. It also lists the claims that arrived without a denominator or a period. The verdict scale and the procedure come from the case report AI Call Center Supervisor in a Live Company (payrollburn, part 1 of the series AI managers in a live company, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23926850), in which only one of nine checkable claims of the agent's own weekly report held exactly as written. The example data are synthetic. Python 3.10+, standard library only, no network calls. Part of the free Digital employees catalog at arsentev.ai/employees.

title: An Improved EfficientNet-B0 Model for Facial Emotion Recognition
abstract: Abstract Facial emotion recognition (FER) is increasingly built into interactive software, but reported accuracies are hard to compare because datasets, emotion sets and evaluation splits differ between studies, and few studies examine whether a larger backbone is worth its extra computational cost on the same data. This study develops and evaluates an EfficientNet-B0 model for five-class FER (happiness, sadness, anger, surprise and neutral) and compares it with EfficientNet-B1 and EfficientNet-B2 trained on the same images. FER2013 and the Real-world Affective Faces Database (RAF-DB) were combined, 1,470 duplicate or label-conflicting images and 19 unreadable files were removed, and a balanced set of 25,000 grayscale images (5,000 per class) was divided into 20,000 training, 2,500 validation and 2,500 test images, with no image shared between subsets. The model was fine-tuned in two stages from ImageNet weights using label smoothing, geometric and photometric augmentation, Mixup and CutMix. On the independent test set, EfficientNet-B0 achieved an accuracy of 78.68%, a macro F1-score of 78.83% and a macro-averaged ROC-AUC of 0.948, with class F1-scores ranging from 70.13% (neutral) to 87.78% (surprise). EfficientNet-B1 reached 79.76% accuracy, a difference that McNemar's test did not find significant (p = 0.107), while EfficientNet-B2, trained under a reduced schedule, reached 75.44% and was significantly less accurate (p < 0.001). EfficientNet-B0 used 36.6% fewer parameters than B1 (4.38 million against 6.90 million), needed 8.5 ms per image for single-image inference against 12.4 ms, required 40% less fine-tuning time and recorded the highest macro AUC of the three backbones. The trained model was deployed in a FastAPI web application that returns the predicted emotion with a confidence score. Within the conditions tested, EfficientNet-B0 gave the best balance between recognition performance and computational cost, while sadness and neutral remained the expressions most often confused with each other.

title: A Metalinguistic Axiomatic Theory of Intelligent Systems: Formal Structures of Cognition, Knowledge, and Theoretical Systems
abstract: English abstractThis work develops a metalinguistic axiomatic framework for cognition, knowledge, theories, intelligent systems, and AI. At the cognitive level, the framework distinguishes objectified items, registered meta-level interfaces, and residual metalanguage, retaining failure and unevaluability. Evaluation, object admission, name binding, and state writeback each have separate conditions. At the knowledge level, knowledge-base membership is distinct from verified or assertable status. Provenance, composite status, four-valued judgment, argumentation, tracing, and safe introduction serve distinct roles. At the theory level, theory objects comprise object and relation sets under co-rootedness and well-founded dependency conditions. Theory evaluation, transformation, and positioning have separate conditional interfaces. At the intelligent-system level, maintenance constrains optimization. Boundary, stable, and higher-order intelligence depend on stated criteria; AI generation and model scale alone do not establish these qualifications. Behavioral interfaces conditionally connect complete action, interaction goals and evaluations, and traceable joint descriptions. A six-step metatheoretical workflow organizes the deconstruction, reconnection, and reconstruction of existing theories. Task-relative textual and geometric representations organize theoretical expression and retrieval without replacing the underlying theory texts. The contribution combines theory-internal axiomatic or quasi-axiomatic reconstruction with cross-level interface organization. It makes domains, dependencies, admissibility, failures, and theoretical effects explicit. Empirical scales, engineering realizations, and system effectiveness require independent implementation and testing.中文摘要认知、知识、理论、智能系统与人工智能研究常使用相互分离的概念语言。产生结果与引入对象、保存信息与接受知识、改善输出与维持系统等不同任务,也因此容易混淆。本文建立一套元语言公理化框架,通过对象层与元层接口连接这些研究层次。框架区分已对象化项目、已登记元语言接口,以及当前对象语言不能吸收的元语言余项,并保留失败与不可评价。 在认知与知识方面,框架分别规定求值、对象引入、名称绑定与状态写回的资格。知识库成员不等于已验证或可断言知识。来源、复合知识标签、主显示、四值判断、论证、回溯和安全引入各有职责;它们不构成所有候选必经的流水线。 在理论层,理论由对象集及其中的关系对象集构成,对象集须满足共根与依赖良基条件。原始对象与基本原理由内部前驱读取,理论品质、变换和结构位置则通过各自的条件接口处理。 在系统层,维持约束优化,边界、稳定和高阶智能按明示判据区分。AI的生成与规模本身不证明这些资格成立。行为附录通过条件接口接入完整行为结构、互动目标与评估,以及可追溯的联合描述。行为分类不等同于趋人化或主体资格。 前四章的部分接口被组织为六步流程,并由四组异质方法示例说明。收束命题仅在各步资格与输入输出条件成立时连接环节;示例本身不独立证明这些条件。第8章规定任务相关的文本与几何表示,并区分假设与待定承接位。索引调用受答案覆盖、局部正确性和完整成本约束。 本文结合选定概念的理论内重建与跨层接口组织,明确各项内容的对象域或元层角色、资格、依赖、失败值与理论效力。工程实现、经验量尺和系统效果仍需独立实现与检验。 Full texts and supplementary materialThis record provides the full text in English and Chinese, together with separate English and bilingual Chinese-English theory-framework diagrams to support reading and cross-referencing of the main text. title: Fooling Deep Neural Networks: A Strategyfor Mitigating DLSCA
abstract: Side-channel analysis (SCA), particularly deep learning-based SCA (DLSCA), threatens cryptographic implementations by automatically exploiting complex and nonlinear leakage and weakening countermeasures such as masking. Existing countermeasures against DLSCA mainly suppress, decorrelate, or obscure exploitable leakage. This work introduces Spoofing-based Mitigation (SPM), a leakage-shaping approach designed to mislead key-recovery attacks by biasing their key hypotheses. SPM introduces a controllable offset into AES intermediate-value computations and compensates for it to preserve the correct ciphertext, while shaping the relationship between measured leakage and the intermediate-value labels used for profiling. We implement SPM at the first-round S-box output and evaluate it at first-round and last-round attack points on an XMEGA128D4 microcontroller using a ChipWhisperer platform. Under the evaluated identity-label settings, the induced key’s rank rapidly reaches zero across seven CNN-based DLSCA models, two MLP-based models, and a template attack, while the correct key remains unrecovered. These results provide experimental evidence that leakage shaping can misdirect the evaluated key-recovery attacks. The collected dataset is publicly available to support reproducible research.

title: A Semantic Representation Model for Geographic Features with Integrated Neighborhood Context
abstract: Geospatial data contains abundant temporal, spatial, and attribute information related to geographic entities, serving as a critical foundation for the development of new quality productive forces. Achieving effective semantic representation of geographic features is a key prerequisite for enabling intelligent data analysis and application. Spatial relationships are an essential semantic characteristic of geographic features and are among the most commonly introduced characteristics for representation learning in recent studies. However, current research primarily focuses on point-based features (such as POIs) or on converting line and polygon features into point features, leading to inaccuracies in representing spatial proximity between features, which in turn affects the representation outcomes. In this paper, a feature unit delineation method based on geometric shapes is proposed to better construct the proximity relationship graph between features. It enriches the semantic features of feature units using a large language model and trains an edge optimization model to refine the graph structure. Building upon iGCL, a semantic representation learning model for geographic features is constructed. Finally, using Xiamen Island and Nanchang City as study areas, experimental datasets are built by integrating OSM and Amap (Gaode) POI data. The performance of the proposed model is validated and compared with other models through three tasks: semantic overlap calculation, node classification, and node clustering. The results show that the feature representations obtained by the proposed model achieve the best performance across all tasks, fully demonstrating its effectiveness and superiority in geographic feature representation learning, thereby providing a foundation for subsequent intelligent geographic feature tasks.
